rule_based_system.summary: An ordered list of IF-THEN rules over grounded market predicates; the first rule that fires decides, with its training up-rate.
rule_based_system.implementationNote: Bridge: first-match decision list; P(up) is the fired rule's smoothed training up-rate (default rule: the base rate), calibrated on validation. Differs from the spec: authored TA rules from cycle_rules.json plus rules mined on the training span, since no expert rule base exists for this market. Expect: coarse, step-like probabilities; coverage depends on how often the rules fire.

induced_feature_count.label: Induced feature predicates
induced_feature_count.description: Feature columns turned into two predicates each (above the training 2/3 quantile, below the 1/3 quantile), chosen by how differently their tails moved on the training span.

atom_order.label: Conditions per mined rule
atom_order.description: Largest number of predicates in one mined rule (1: single conditions, 2: pairs).

minimum_fire_count.label: Minimum firings
minimum_fire_count.description: A mined rule must have fired on at least this many training bars.

rule_count.label: Rules kept
rule_count.description: Rules kept after ranking by how far their training up-rate sits from the base rate.

smoothing_pseudo_count.label: Smoothing pseudo-count
smoothing_pseudo_count.description: Pseudo-bars at the base rate added to every training rate (Laplace-style smoothing).

native.produces: One deterministic action per bar, taken from the first rule in a fixed priority list whose condition is true on that bar's facts, together with the name of the rule that fired, or a fixed default action when no rule matches.
native.targetVariable: The trading action for the current bar (for example enter long, reduce size or hold) chosen by the highest-priority matching condition; it is a decision, not a statement about the size or probability of the coming move.
native.objectiveNote: Nothing is minimised: a person authors the conditions and their priority order and checks the fixed list against history; as run by the Model Cycle the rule set is the authored technical-analysis rules in cycle_rules.json plus rules mined on each fold's training span.

metrics.why: Because the list stops at the first matching condition, the share of bars decided by a real rule instead of the default action, and the share each rule claims before the ones below it get a turn, shows whether the priority order leaves the lower rules any bars at all.

Each rule is a yes-or-no test with no confidence attached, so the only evidence that it knows something is that the bars it fired on were followed by a different up share than the series as a whole, counted on bars after the ones its thresholds were tuned on.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series over the same span.

metrics.why: The list outputs an action, hold included, so its own decisions are replayed on later bars after costs and read against doing nothing, which is the reference the specification itself names for a rule stack.
metrics.baseline: Taking no action on the same bars, which earns zero.

metrics.why: Every threshold nudged and every reordering tried against the same backtest window is one more attempt, and a hand-tuned cutoff looks better the more versions were tried, so the count of rule versions tested is reported beside the result.

When the thresholds are recalibrated on the next trailing window, a rule that keeps its cutoff and its place in the priority order is a durable condition, while one that has to be rewritten each time was fitted to one stretch of history.

notApplicable.why: It never applied: a priority-ordered rule list has no density and no hidden states, so no log-likelihood exists for it.

notApplicable.name: Regime Separation Index
notApplicable.why: It never applied: the list builds no volatility clusters, and the registry has no such metric; the outcome separation per fired rule takes its place.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: It never applied: it describes a hyperparameter search, and a hand-authored rule list has none natively.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: It never applied: the fired rule is the whole explanation, so there are no Shapley importances to rank across folds.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: It never applied natively: the specification states that rules carry no certainty factor or probability, so there are no odds to calibrate.

notApplicable.name: Regime Persistence Ratio
notApplicable.why: It never applied: there is no Markov transition matrix whose diagonal could be read, because each bar is decided on its own.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Natively the output is an action and a rule name, not a probability of up; the probability scored by the Model Cycle is added by a bridge.

notApplicable.name: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
notApplicable.why: A list of a few rules gives a few output levels, so the ranking curve has only a few points and cannot be the headline number.

asRun.standInNote: The specification describes a list of conditions and actions authored and ordered by an expert; the runnable adapter instead offers the authored technical-analysis rules in cycle_rules.json as candidates beside single conditions and pairs mined on the fold's training span, ranks all candidates by the standardised gap between each rule's smoothed training up-rate and the training base rate (a gap that grows with the number of times the rule fired), keeps only the highest ranked up to the rule count so an authored rule can be dropped, and turns the fired rule's up-rate into a probability of up through a logistic curve fitted on validation bars, so every as-run number measures that mined and reordered list plus the curve, not an expert's rule base choosing actions.
asRun.probabilityNote: Each bar walks the ordered list, the first rule whose every condition is true supplies the log-odds of its smoothed training up-rate (the training base rate when no rule fires), and the probability of up is an unweighted logistic curve of that value fitted on the fold's validation bars.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: It grades the stated odds of the fired rule's up-rate after the validation curve on test bars, so it shows whether the up-rates counted on the training span still hold, read against quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.

The call flips when the curve-mapped probability of the fired rule's up-rate crosses one half, which can sit at an up-rate other than one half because the curve is fitted on validation bars, so the profit after costs shows whether the handful of rules that move the call away from the side of the default rule were worth trading under the engine's rule.
The list gives a small set of probability levels, one per rule plus the default, and the bounded squared-error score grades those levels without being dominated by a few confident bars.
The curve is unweighted, so its odds are comparable with observed up shares, but the few rule levels fill only a few of the ten bins, so it is read with the occupied-bin count.

A slope well below one on test bars means the rules' training up-rates were stretched further from the base rate than the later bars support, which is the expected mark of rules picked for their extreme training rates.

It asks whether bars under rules with higher up-rates went up more often than bars under rules with lower ones, but with one level per rule the curve has only a few points, so it is supporting evidence only.

The number of levels can be at most the number of rules kept plus the default, and when most bars fall to the default rule it shows that the ranking and calibration numbers rest on very few distinct outputs.

It counts how often the side chosen by the fired rule's curve-mapped up-rate matched the move; bars under the default rule all share the curve value of the training base rate, so they take one fixed side that the validation-fitted curve decides, not the training base rate directly.
Because the default rule sends every uncovered bar to the same side, the average of the up recall and the down recall shows whether the fired rules add anything beyond calling the majority direction.
It is near zero when the list almost always answers with the default side and rises only if the bars moved to the other side by a fired rule were moved correctly.
It relates the per-bar profit of trading the rule list's call to its variability, and a list that mostly sits on the default side inherits the risk of simply holding that side.
A step-like call holds one side for long stretches until a rule on the other side fires, so the deepest equity fall shows the cost of those long holds when the market runs against the default side.

Bars under the default rule all take one fixed side that the validation-fitted curve decides from the training base rate, so the profit beyond holding the contract isolates what the rules that fire contribute, and it reads as a gap to holding only when that fixed side is long.
It compares the dollars won and lost on the trades opened when a fired rule flips the call, which are few when the rules rarely disagree with the default side.
A trade closes only when a rule on the opposite side fires or the fold ends, so the share of winning trades describes those flips and must be read with the trade count.
The number of closed trades equals the number of times the first matching rule changed the side of the call, which shows how often the list really speaks.
It shows how one-sided the list is; a share at or near one or zero means the default rule and the base rate are making nearly every call.
Every single condition and every pair of conditions is scored on the training span before the strongest are kept, so this count is the multiple-testing exposure behind the kept rules' up-rates.
The search over rule count, conditions per rule, minimum firings and smoothing is scored by the shared tuning objective, an optimistic selection score to be read beside the fold's test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: Not computed: this model has no price model, so no forecast line is drawn and no forecast error exists.
Not computed: the decision list forecasts no move size, so there is no error in points to report.
Not computed: with no price model there is no forecast sign to compare with the actual move.
Nothing is minimised and the fit is a single count of rule up-rates that returns no loss, so no training value is reported to subtract from the validation logarithmic loss.
With long-only off and no stop or target the engine is always in the market once the first call is made, so the share describes the engine's rule and not the rule list.

caveats: The rule set is the authored technical-analysis rules in cycle_rules.json plus rules mined on the fold's training span; the authored rules are only candidates that are ranked and capped together with the mined ones, so they are not guaranteed a place in the list, and the order is the standardised gap between each rule's smoothed training up-rate and the training base rate, which also grows with the number of firings, so a frequent rule with a modest gap can outrank a rare rule with an extreme rate; it is not an order authored by an expert.

Each kept rule's up-rate is counted on the same training bars that were used to pick it as one of the strongest, so the rates are optimistic by selection and the smoothing pseudo-count only partly corrects this.
The single fit logs one validation logarithmic loss for the epoch, measured on the same validation bars the logistic curve was fitted on, and no training value because the rule counts return no loss.
The logistic curve's slope and intercept are fitted on the validation bars, and if the fitted slope is negative a rule with a high training up-rate is traded as a down call.
A condition whose input is unknown on a bar never fires, so early bars of a fold fall to the default rule more often than later ones.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than MNQ the cost per side is the MNQ account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

expert_system.summary: Forward chaining over a working memory of graded facts with MYCIN certainty factors: pattern rules assert setups, hypothesis rules turn them into belief in an up move.
expert_system.implementationNote: Bridge: MYCIN forward chaining (recognise-act cycles, refraction, certainty combination); the final certainty of 'up' is mapped to P(up) by a validation curve. Differs from the spec: rule certainty factors are calibrated on the training span (MB/MD from training up-rates) instead of elicited from an expert. Expect: probabilities near the base rate unless strong patterns fire together.

atom_order.label: Conditions per mined rule
atom_order.description: Largest number of predicates in one mined rule (1: single conditions, 2: pairs).

minimum_fire_count.description: A mined rule must have fired on at least this many training bars.

certainty_threshold.label: Certainty threshold
certainty_threshold.description: A rule fires only when its premise certainty is at least this (MYCIN uses 0.2).

maximum_inference_cycles.label: Inference cycles
maximum_inference_cycles.description: Recognise-act cycles before inference stops (two are needed to reach a hypothesis).

native.produces: A set of derived facts, usually a trade recommendation, each carrying the combined certainty factor of the chain of rules that fired to reach it.
native.targetVariable: The recommendation an expert's production rules reach from the current bar's observed facts, with a heuristic certainty between minus one and one
native.objectiveNote: The rule base and its certainty factors are authored by a domain expert; the only fitting the specification allows is nudging each certainty factor toward the rule's historical hit rate on a trailing window, which is counting, not loss minimisation.

metrics.why: Forward chaining only speaks on bars where some production rule's premise clears the certainty threshold, so the share of bars that end with a conclusion in working memory, and the share each rule fires on, shows how much of the tape the knowledge base actually covers.

Each fired rule chain is a claim that the market behaves differently after it, so the up share of the bars where the chain concluded up is compared with the up share of all bars of the same series, one row per rule.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: When certainty factors are recalibrated on each trailing window, this shows how often the same rules keep the same sign of certainty, which separates stable desk knowledge from a rule that only worked in one window.

Every rule whose certainty factor was checked against history is one more chance for a lucky hit rate, so the number of rules tried before the knowledge base was frozen is shown beside any rule that looks strong.

notApplicable.name: Regime Log-Likelihood
notApplicable.why: The rule base assigns certainty factors, not probability densities, and has no regimes, so this row never described an expert system.

notApplicable.name: Regime Separation Index
notApplicable.why: Production rules and working memory define no regimes, so a separation index has nothing to act on.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: An authored rule base has no hyperparameter search whose variance could be decomposed.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: The fired rule chain is the explanation, so attribution stability is not a quantity this model has.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: A certainty factor is not a probability, so natively its calibration against frequency is undefined; the outcome separation per fired rule is the native outcome check kept instead.

notApplicable.name: Regime Persistence Ratio
notApplicable.why: There is no regime state in a forward-chaining engine whose persistence could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
notApplicable.why: As a headline it misleads, because every bar on which no rule concluded shares the single combined certainty of zero, so the ranking is decided only by the bars where a rule chain fired and the tied bars carry no order among themselves.

asRun.standInNote: The inference engine is the specification's own: forward chaining over a working memory with recognise-act cycles, refraction, priority ordering and the MYCIN combination function. What differs is the knowledge: the pattern rules are the authored technical-analysis rules plus conjunctions mined on the training span, and each rule's certainty factor is computed from its training up share against the base rate instead of being elicited from an expert, and the final certainty of up is turned into a probability by a logistic curve fitted on validation rows.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is an unweighted logistic curve, fitted by maximum likelihood on the fold's validation rows only, of the final combined certainty factor of the fact up in working memory, which is zero on bars where no rule concluded.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per scored validation bar, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: The curve is unweighted, so this grades the odds that come from the combined certainty of up plus the validation-fitted slope and intercept, against quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.
A monotone curve leaves the ranking untouched, so this tests the chained certainty itself: do bars with a higher combined certainty of up go up more often, with all no-conclusion bars tied at zero.
A bounded score of the curve-mapped certainty, less dominated than the logarithmic loss by the few bars where several strong rules fire together.

The MYCIN combination adds certainty with every agreeing rule, so a slope below one on the test span means the chain stacked more confidence than the outcomes supported even after the validation curve.
The unweighted curve anchors the odds to the validation up share, so the binned gap fairly checks certainty plus curve, though most bars sit in the bins around the base rate.
What trading the sign of the curve-mapped certainty earned after costs, including the bars with no conclusion, where the curve's intercept alone decides the side.
Return per unit of bar-to-bar swing from following the expert system's call; zero is an arithmetic marker because a random side still pays costs.
The deepest equity fall while following the rule chain's call, which shows the losing stretch a trader would have endured.
Winning dollars over losing dollars across trades opened when the chained conclusion flipped side; one is an arithmetic marker only.
Share of closed trades that made money when the side came from the fired rule chain, read with the trade count because calls flip only when the conclusion changes.
Hit rate of the call cut at 0.5; on bars where no rule fired it is the validation intercept's guess, so it mixes the knowledge base with the prior.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and down bars, so the many no-conclusion bars all called the same side cannot lift the number through the base rate.
One symmetric number for whether the rule chain's call agrees with the realised direction; it sits near zero when most bars get the intercept's side.

Every single predicate, and every pair when the atom order parameter allows pairs, is scored on the training span before the strongest become pattern rules, so this count is the multiple-testing exposure of the knowledge base.
Shows how far the fired chains ever move the odds from the base rate; the registry note says to expect little unless strong patterns fire together.

Holding the contract through the same folds is the only same-series trading reference, so this gap shows whether trading the side of the combined certainty earned more than simply holding, after the costs that every flip of the conclusion pays.

A trade closes only when the sign of the curve-mapped combined certainty changes, so this count shows how often the fired rule chains actually changed the side, and every trading figure for this model is read beside it.

Shows how one-sided the combined certainty plus the validation-fitted curve is; a share at or near one or zero means the curve's intercept, which decides every bar with no conclusion, is making nearly every call.

The search over the induced feature count, the atom order, the minimum fire count, the rule count, the smoothing pseudo count and the certainty threshold is scored by the shared tuning objective, an optimistic selection score to be read beside the fold's test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: Not computed: this model has no price model, because forward chaining concludes only a certainty of up.
Not computed: this model has no price model, so there is no forecast move to compare with the actual move.
Not computed: this model has no price model, so there is no forecast sign to score.

The combined certainty varies continuously on bars where a rule chain fires, because each fact's certainty comes from a smooth truth degree, and it ties at zero only on bars with no conclusion, so a level count does not describe how coarse the ranking is.
Forward chaining counts rule hit rates and returns no training loss, so no training value is recorded to subtract from the single validation logarithmic loss.

With long only off and no stop or target the engine is always in a position, so the specification's certainty threshold for acting never keeps the trader flat and exposure describes the engine's rule.

caveats: The single fit logs one validation logarithmic loss for the epoch, measured on the same validation rows that fitted the curve's slope and intercept, and no training value because forward chaining returns no loss.
The curve's slope and intercept were fitted on validation rows, so every probability metric grades certainty plus curve, and a negative fitted slope would trade against the rule chain.
The certainty threshold gates which rules may fire, not whether a trade is taken: a bar with no conclusion is still traded on the side the curve's intercept gives.
Rule certainty factors come from training-span up shares of mined patterns, so they carry the selection luck of every candidate rule that was scored.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost per side is that contract's account figure, a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

probabilistic_logic_network.summary: Truth values with strength and evidence count; implication links from predicates to an up move are chained by PLN deduction and merged by revision.
probabilistic_logic_network.implementationNote: Bridge: PLN deduction and revision over training-span truth values; P(up) = confidence x strength + (1 - confidence) x base rate, then a validation curve. Differs from the spec: atoms are the bar's grounded predicates and concepts are mined rules, not an AtomSpace; deduction assumes independent links. Expect: estimates close to the base rate when evidence is thin.

induced_feature_count.description: Feature columns turned into two predicates each (above the training 2/3 quantile, below the 1/3 quantile), chosen by how differently their tails moved on the training span.

atom_order.label: Conditions per mined rule
atom_order.description: Largest number of predicates in one mined rule (1: single conditions, 2: pairs).

minimum_fire_count.label: Minimum firings
minimum_fire_count.description: A mined rule must have fired on at least this many training bars.

smoothing_pseudo_count.label: Smoothing pseudo-count
smoothing_pseudo_count.description: Pseudo-bars at the base rate added to every training rate (Laplace-style smoothing).

evidence_scale.label: Evidence scale
evidence_scale.description: k in confidence = n / (n + k): how many observations make a link trustworthy.

maximum_chain_depth.label: Chain depth
maximum_chain_depth.description: 1: direct links only; 2: one deduction through a concept; 3: through two concepts.

native.produces: A truth value for the queried trading proposition made of two numbers: a strength, which is the estimated probability that the proposition holds, and a confidence, which says how much counted evidence stands behind that strength.
native.targetVariable: Whether the queried proposition (for example that the up move continues) is true for the current bar, given the evidence atoms observed on that bar
native.objectiveNote: Nothing is minimised: each implication link gets its strength from a historical frequency count and its confidence from the size of that count, and the deduction and revision formulas then combine those counted truth values by fixed arithmetic.

metrics.why: The strength that comes out of the deduction and revision chain is offered as a probability for the queried proposition, so the honest test is how much probability it placed on what the next bars actually did.
metrics.baseline: Quoting the fold's training up share on every scored bar, which is exactly what the network returns when its confidence is zero

metrics.why: A bounded second opinion on the revised strength, useful because confidence shrinkage keeps most answers close to the base rate where the logarithmic score barely moves.
metrics.baseline: The same score for quoting the fold's training up share on every scored bar

metrics.why: The deduction formula assumes the chained links are independent and revision adds their evidence counts together, so correlated indicators get counted twice and the merged strength can sit further from the base rate than the bars justify; a slope below one shows that.

Each implication link claims a strength for an up move when its atom is true, so on unseen bars the up share among the bars where that atom held should sit on the same side of the series' up share as the stored strength.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: The knowledge base is a set of implication links whose strengths are re-counted on every fold, so a link whose strength changes side of the base rate from one training span to the next was never knowledge about this market.

On a bar where no evidence atom is true there is no derivation to revise and the network can only repeat the base rate, so the share of bars with at least one true atom says how often it reasoned at all.

The strength is meant to be read as a frequency, so binning the answers and comparing each bin with what happened is a fair picture of it, read together with how few bins the base-rate-hugging answers occupy.

The evidence scale constant decides how fast confidence rises with the evidence count, and a large constant pulls every answer back to the base rate, so the spread of the answers shows whether the network ever commits.

notApplicable.name: Regime Log-Likelihood
notApplicable.why: It scores a hidden-state mixture density, and this model stores counted truth values on implication links with no hidden states and no density.

notApplicable.name: Regime Separation Index
notApplicable.why: It measures the distance between volatility clusters, and this model forms no clusters; its atoms are named predicates that are true or false on a bar.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: It attributes search-score variance to hyperparameters, which describes a tuning study and says nothing about whether the inferred strengths are right.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: Shapley attributions explain a fitted function of feature columns, while this model's explanation is the inference chain itself; the stability question is asked of the links through structure stability instead.

notApplicable.name: Regime Persistence Ratio
notApplicable.why: It reads the diagonal of a Markov transition matrix, and this model has no transition matrix and no regime that carries over between bars.

notApplicable.name: Solver convergence residual
notApplicable.why: Forward chaining to a fixed chain depth is finite arithmetic on truth values and never iterates toward a fixed point, so there is no residual to watch.

notApplicable.name: Mean test-tape return of the model's own action
notApplicable.why: The network answers how likely a proposition is and contains no decision or utility node, so it never chooses an action whose reward could be summed.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable engine applies the specification's own deduction formula, count-pooling revision and the confidence rule built on evidence_scale, but the atoms are grounded predicates on this instrument's indicators and feature columns, the intermediate concepts are rule conjunctions mined on the fold's training span instead of an authored knowledge base, induction and abduction are absent, and a logistic curve fitted on validation bars sits between the inferred strength and the probability that is scored and traded; every as-run number therefore measures counted links plus that curve.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each bar the evidence of its true atoms is pooled into one strength and one count, the strength is shrunk toward the training up share by the confidence that count earns under evidence_scale, the log-odds of the result is the score, and an unweighted logistic curve fitted on the fold's validation bars turns that score into the probability of up.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit, validation rows only

meaningful.why: It grades the revised and confidence-shrunk strength after the validation curve has rescaled it, on test bars neither the counts nor the curve have seen, so it tests whether counted implication links carry over to new bars.

The validation curve only stretches and shifts the score, so the ordering of bars is the network's own pooled strength, and this number asks whether bars with stronger pooled evidence for up went up more often.
A bounded proper score for the curve-mapped strength, which matters here because confidence shrinkage keeps most probabilities near the training up share where logarithmic loss changes very little.

Neither the counted strengths nor the validation curve are class weighted, so the probability is aimed at the true up frequency and the binned gap tests whether the curve fitted on validation bars still holds on test bars.

Revision adds evidence counts from indicators that move together as if they were independent witnesses, and a slope away from one on test bars shows how much of that double counting the validation curve failed to undo.

A bar with few true atoms earns little confidence and is answered with almost the training up share, so the spread of the probabilities shows how often the network had enough evidence to move away from it.
Each distinct set of true atoms gives one pooled strength, so the number of levels shows whether the ranking metrics rest on a fine ordering or on a handful of atom combinations.

The up or down call cuts the curve-mapped strength at one half, so it tests the network's ordering together with the intercept the validation curve chose, and should be read against the majority-class accuracy.
Because shrinkage holds most probabilities on one side of one half, the network can call nearly every bar the same way, and averaging the two recalls exposes that where plain accuracy hides it.
One number over all four confusion cells that falls to zero when the base-rate-hugging probabilities put every call on the same side, which is the usual failure of this network.
Shows how lopsided the calls are once probabilities cluster around the training up share, which decides whether the trading numbers describe the network or simply one held position.
What following the side of one half that the curve-mapped strength falls on earned after costs under the engine's position rule, to be read beside buy and hold on the same folds.
The steadiness of that profit per bar; when the calls rarely flip it mostly describes the instrument's own path over the fold, so it is read with the predicted up share and trade count.
The deepest loss run of the position the network's calls held, a property of how seldom the pooled evidence changes its mind as much as of the calls being wrong.
Winning against losing trade totals for trades that open and close when the pooled strength crosses one half, meaningful only when the trade count shows the call actually flipped.
The share of profitable trades opened by a flip of the call, which says how often a change in the true atoms was followed by a move large enough to cover costs.
Counts how often the curve-mapped strength crossed one half, which for a network that answers near the base rate can be a very small number behind every trading metric.

Not computed: no price model is fitted beside the network, so there is no forecast move to compare with the actual move.

The single counting pass returns no training loss, so the one epoch reports a validation loss only, and that value is scored on the same bars the validation curve was fitted on, so there is no training value to subtract and the validation value is in-sample for the curve.
With long only switched off and no stop or target set the engine is always in the market once it has traded, so the figure describes the engine's rule and not the network.

The feature-column predicates are chosen by how differently their tails moved on the training span and the concepts are the highest-ranked mined conjunctions, so the stored strengths are the best of many candidates and are optimistic on the training bars.
The deduction formula treats the two links of a chain as independent and a two-step chain is counted at half its co-occurrence evidence, which is an engine choice and not part of the specification.

atom_order.label: Conditions per mined rule

minimum_fire_count.label: Minimum firings

epochs.label: Epochs

learning_rate.label: Learning rate

native.produces: A continuous truth value between zero and one for every queried target atom, found as the jointly most probable assignment of a hinge-loss Markov random field built from weighted soft-logic rules.
native.targetVariable: The degree to which the target atom (for example that the move continues) is true for the current market snapshot, given the graded truth of the observed atoms
native.objectiveNote: Inference minimises the weighted sum of each grounded rule's distance to satisfaction, which is convex, and weight learning moves each rule weight so that the observed outcome has lower energy than the inferred one.

metrics.why: The inferred truth of the target atom is a graded degree and not a stated frequency, so the first question is whether bars given a higher truth of up really went up more often than bars given a lower one.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value for a truth degree that orders up bars and down bars no better than chance

metrics.why: The squared gap between the inferred truth and the outcome is the structured loss the weights are learned against, and it stays finite when the linear hinge puts the inferred truth exactly at zero or one.
metrics.baseline: The same score for quoting the fold's training up share on every scored bar

metrics.why: A weighted rule base is used to pick out the bars where many rule bodies are strongly satisfied, so the precision among the highest inferred truths tests the part of the output a desk would act on.
metrics.baseline: The up share of the scored bars, which is what a truth degree with no ordering power gives

metrics.why: Each rule states that a satisfied body should be followed by its head, so on unseen bars the up share where a rule's body was strongly true should differ from the series' up share in the direction the rule concludes.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: A rule weight driven to zero has been rejected by the data, so the set of rules that keep a positive weight is the learned structure, and a rule that survives in one fold and dies in the next carries no dependable weight.

The consensus solver that finds the most probable assignment runs inside every weight-learning step, and a weight update taken against an assignment that had not settled pushes a biased gradient into the rule weights.

On a bar where every rule body has zero truth only the prior rules act and the inferred truth is the same constant, so the share of bars with at least one active body says how often the rule base spoke.

notApplicable.name: Regime Separation Index

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss of the raw truth value
notApplicable.why: The inferred truth is a degree of satisfaction that the linear hinge can place exactly at zero or one, where the logarithmic score is unbounded; it becomes gradeable only after a curve maps the degree to a probability.

notApplicable.name: Mean test-tape return of the model's own action
notApplicable.why: The rule base infers how true a proposition is and contains no decision node, so it selects no action whose reward could be summed.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable engine keeps the specification's Lukasiewicz rule bodies, hinge-loss energy, non-negative learned weights and exact most probable assignment, but each bar has a single free atom (the truth of up, with down as its complement), so the alternating direction method of multipliers and joint inference across related atoms never run; the rules are conjunctions mined on the fold's training span plus the authored rule library, the weights are learned by a structured perceptron step, and a logistic curve fitted on validation bars turns the inferred truth into the probability that is scored and traded.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each bar the engine finds the truth of up that exactly minimises the weighted hinge-loss energy of the mined and authored rules plus two prior rules, takes the log-odds of that truth as the score, and an unweighted logistic curve refitted on the fold's validation bars at every epoch maps the score to the probability of up.

stepQuantity.unit: squared truth units on training bars and nats on validation bars

meaningful.why: The validation curve only stretches and shifts the score, so the ordering of test bars is the inferred truth of up itself, and this asks whether bars whose weighted rule bodies pushed that truth higher went up more often.

The squared gap between probability and outcome is the same kind of loss the weight learning reports on training bars, here taken on test bars after the curve, and it is not the quantity the kept epoch was chosen on.

It grades the inferred truth after the curve has turned it into odds; the kept epoch is the one with the lowest value of this same loss on validation bars, so the test value is honest but the validation value is optimistic.
Looks at the bars with the highest inferred truth, where several up-concluding rule bodies were strongly satisfied at once, and asks how many of those really went up.

The perceptron step and the curve are both unweighted, so the probability aims at the true up frequency, and the binned gap tests whether the curve chosen on validation bars still maps truth degrees to frequencies on test bars.
With the linear hinge the minimising truth sits at zero, one, a rule body or its complement, so many bars share a level and the ranking metrics can rest on a short staircase.
When the two prior rules outweigh the mined rules the inferred truth barely moves from bar to bar and the curve returns almost one value, which a spread near zero reveals.
The call cuts the curve-mapped truth at one half, so it tests the rule vote together with the intercept the validation curve chose, and is read against the majority-class accuracy.
The curve's intercept can place every truth level on the same side of one half, and averaging the two recalls shows whether the weighted rules ever change the call.
One number over all four confusion cells that falls to zero when the learned weights leave the call on one side for the whole fold.
What following the side of one half that the curve-mapped truth falls on earned after costs under the engine's position rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds.
The steadiness of that profit per bar for a position that changes only when the weighted rule vote crosses the curve's midpoint, read with the trade count.
The deepest loss run of the position the soft rule vote held, which lengthens when the rule bodies stay satisfied through a move against them.
Winning against losing trade totals for trades opened when the inferred truth crosses the curve's midpoint, meaningful only when the trade count shows it crossed often enough.
The share of profitable trades opened by a change in which rule bodies are satisfied, which says how often such a change was followed by a move that covered costs.
Shows whether the prior rules and the curve's intercept have made the engine a one-sided caller, the context needed before reading its trading numbers.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: Not computed: the registry gives this model no price block, and a truth degree for up says nothing about the size of the move.
Not computed: no price model is fitted beside the rule base, so there is no forecast move to compare with the actual move.
Not computed: with no price forecast there is no forecast sign; the direction call is scored by the classification metrics.

The training channel holds the squared gap between the uncalibrated inferred truth and the outcome while the validation channel holds the logarithmic loss of the curve-mapped probability, so the two are different quantities and their difference means nothing.
With long only switched off and no stop or target set the engine is always in the market once it has traded, so the figure describes the engine's rule and not the rule base.
Its reference is the test bars' own up share known only in hindsight, while the engine's prior rules start from the training up share, so the comparison is not the one the model makes.

caveats: The logistic curve is refitted on the fold's validation bars at every epoch and the epoch kept is the one with the lowest logarithmic loss on those same bars, so the validation loss is in-sample for the curve and optimistic through the selection.
The curve's slope is not forced to be positive, so a validation span on which a higher inferred truth was followed by down moves inverts the rule vote for the whole test span.

The logged training loss is the squared gap between the inferred truth and the outcome, which is not the hinge-loss energy difference the structured perceptron step actually follows, so the training curve is a progress trace and not the objective.

The rules are the highest-ranked conjunctions mined on the fold's training span together with the authored rule library, so the rule set is the best of many candidates and its weights are then learned on the same bars.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so intervals around any score need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than MNQ the cost per side is the MNQ account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

fuzzy_logic_model.summary: Linguistic terms (low / medium / high) on the most informative features, Wang-Mendel rules learned from training bars, Mamdani min-max inference and centroid defuzzification.
fuzzy_logic_model.implementationNote: Bridge: vectorised Mamdani inference (checked against scikit-fuzzy's control system); the centroid bullishness in [-1, 1] becomes P(up) through a validation curve. Differs from the spec: rules are generated from training bars (Wang-Mendel), not written by hand. Expect: smooth but low-resolution scores.

input_feature_count.description: Feature columns used as fuzzy inputs (most training mutual information).

rule_count.label: Rules kept
rule_count.description: Wang-Mendel rules kept, by training degree mass.

defuzzification_grid_points.label: Defuzzification grid
defuzzification_grid_points.description: Points of the output universe the centroid is computed on.

native.produces: One crisp, smoothly varying bullishness signal per bar between minus one and one, the centroid of the fuzzy output set that the fired linguistic rules aggregate into.
native.targetVariable: The graded bullishness the linguistic rule base assigns to the current bar's indicator readings
native.objectiveNote: A hand-authored Mamdani system fits nothing: memberships and rules are written by a person; only the tuned variant, which adjusts triangle vertices and rule weights by gradient descent, minimises a squared error.

metrics.why: Where adjacent membership functions leave a gap no linguistic rule fires and the centroid falls back to neutral, so the share of bars with at least one rule firing above zero strength shows how much of the tape the rule base really grades.

The centroid is a graded opinion, so bars are grouped by bins of the defuzzified bullishness and each bin's up share is compared with the up share of all bars of the same series, which shows whether a higher centroid is really followed by more up moves.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: Unlike a crisp rule list, the defuzzified centroid varies continuously, so its ordering of bars from most bearish to most bullish can be graded without choosing any cut on the signal.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value of a signal that orders up bars and down bars at random

metrics.why: For the tuned variant this shows how often the same membership peaks and the same rule consequents come back when the system is refitted on the next window, which is the difference between a readable rule base and one that is rewritten every period.

The number of antecedent combinations grows with the count of inputs and of terms per input, so the count of rules proposed before the rule base was cut down is shown beside it as its exposure to lucky rules.

notApplicable.why: Fuzzy membership is not probability and the system defines no regimes, so a regime likelihood never applied.

notApplicable.name: Regime Separation Index
notApplicable.why: The linguistic terms are overlapping grades of one input, not regimes of the market, so their separation is not a quality of the model.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: No hyperparameter search exists in an authored fuzzy rule base, so nothing can be attributed to hyperparameters.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: Rule firing strengths are the model's own explanation, so attribution stability is not one of its quantities.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: The defuzzified signal is a score, not a probability, so natively it has no calibration.

notApplicable.name: Regime Persistence Ratio
notApplicable.why: No regime label exists in a fuzzy inference system whose persistence could be counted.

asRun.standInNote: The inference is the specification's own Mamdani system: minimum for conjunction, clipping for implication, maximum for aggregation and a centroid bullishness between minus one and one. What differs is where the knowledge comes from: the inputs are the feature columns with the most mutual information with the training direction, the membership peaks sit at training quantiles, and the rules are generated from training bars by the Wang-Mendel method instead of being written by hand; the centroid is then turned into a probability by a logistic curve fitted on validation rows.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is an unweighted logistic curve, fitted by maximum likelihood on the fold's validation rows only, of the centroid of the aggregated fuzzy output set, which is zero on bars where no generated rule fires.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per scored validation bar, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: The curve is unweighted, so this grades the odds that come from the centroid bullishness plus the validation-fitted slope and intercept, against quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.
The centroid varies smoothly and the curve is monotone, so this ranking score tests the fuzzy signal itself: do bars with a more bullish centroid go up more often.
A bounded score of the curve-mapped centroid, a second view of the same odds that is not dominated by a few confident bars.

Clipping and centroid averaging compress the signal toward neutral, and the curve re-stretches it on validation rows, so a slope away from one on the test span shows that stretch did not carry forward.
The unweighted curve anchors the odds to the validation up share, so the binned gap fairly checks centroid plus curve, though a low-resolution signal fills only the bins near the base rate.
What trading the side of the curve-mapped centroid earned after costs, which also shows whether the smooth signal really avoids the whipsaw the specification says a hard threshold causes.
Return per unit of bar-to-bar swing from following the fuzzy signal's side; zero is an arithmetic marker because a random side still pays costs.
The deepest equity fall while following the centroid's side, the losing stretch a trader of this rule base would have sat through.
Winning dollars over losing dollars across trades opened when the centroid crossed the fitted cut; one is an arithmetic marker only.
Share of closed trades that made money when the side came from the defuzzified signal, read with the trade count.
The specification's selling point is a signal that does not flip back and forth at a boundary, and the number of call flips per session day measures exactly that.
Hit rate of the call cut at 0.5, which places the cut on the centroid wherever the validation curve's intercept puts it rather than at neutral.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and down bars, so a centroid that sits on one side of the fitted cut on most bars cannot score through the base rate.
One symmetric number for whether the side of the centroid agrees with the realised direction across the confusion table.

Every training bar proposes an antecedent and only the ones with the most degree mass are kept, and the inputs themselves were picked by mutual information with the label, so this count is the selection exposure of the rule base.
Shows how far the centroid ever moves the odds from the base rate; the registry note says to expect smooth but low-resolution scores.

Holding the contract through the same folds is the only same-series trading reference, so this gap shows whether trading the side of the curve-mapped centroid earned more than simply holding, after the costs that every crossing of the fitted cut pays.

A trade closes only when the centroid crosses the validation-fitted cut, so this count shows how often the fuzzy signal actually changed the side, and every trading figure for this model is read beside it.

Shows how one-sided the centroid plus the validation-fitted curve is; a share at or near one or zero means the curve's intercept, which decides every bar where no generated rule fires, is making nearly every call.

The search over the input feature count, the membership function count and the rule count is scored by the shared tuning objective, an optimistic selection score to be read beside the fold's test value.

metrics.why: The prover only says something on bars where the empty clause is reached, so the share of bars on which the query is proved, split from the share that hit the resolution step limit, shows how often the knowledge base speaks at all.

This tracks how often the same clauses produce the bindings from one period to the next, which shows whether the answers rest on durable relations or on facts that were true only for a short stretch.

notApplicable.name: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve

asRun.standInNote: The specification returns the variable bindings for which a goal is provable and estimates nothing; the runnable adapter states a small Horn-clause program about nested trends, supporting predicates and fired rules, lets miniKanren enumerate the distinct derivations of the up signal and of the down signal for each bar, and uses the count of up derivations minus down derivations as a score that a validation-fitted curve maps to a probability. miniKanren stands in for a Prolog interpreter, and every as-run number measures that vote-like count difference, not provability.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is an unweighted logistic curve, fitted by maximum likelihood on the fold's validation rows only, of the number of distinct derivations of the up signal minus the number of distinct derivations of the down signal, each capped at the answer limit.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per scored validation bar, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: The curve is unweighted, so this grades the odds that come from the derivation count difference plus the validation-fitted slope and intercept, against quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.
A bounded score of a probability that takes one value per whole-number count difference, which reads cleanly for the stepped output this model gives.
The curve is monotone, so this tests the vote itself: do bars with more up derivations than down derivations go up more often, with ties counted half because the difference is a whole number.
The count difference takes only whole-number values within the answer limit, so this shows how few points the ranking and calibration figures are drawn from.
Nested-window derivations are not independent votes, so a slope below one on the test span means the curve gave each extra derivation more weight than the outcomes supported.
The unweighted curve anchors the odds to the validation up share, so the binned gap fairly checks count difference plus curve, read with the count of occupied bins.
What trading the side with more derivations earned after costs under the engine's rule of following the latest call and filling at the next open.
Return per unit of bar-to-bar swing from trading the side the logic program derives more often; zero is an arithmetic marker because a random side still pays costs.
The deepest equity fall while following the derivation vote, the losing stretch a trader of this program would have sat through.
Winning dollars over losing dollars across trades opened when the derivation vote changed side; one is an arithmetic marker only.
Share of closed trades that made money when the side came from the derivation vote, read with the trade count.
Hit rate of the call cut at 0.5; a tied count is called by the validation intercept, so the number mixes the program with the prior.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and down bars, so the many tied bars all called the same side cannot lift the number through the base rate.
One symmetric number for whether the side with more derivations agrees with the realised direction across the confusion table.

The fired-rule facts come from rules mined over every single predicate, and every pair when the atom order parameter allows pairs, on the training span, so this count is the multiple-testing exposure behind those clauses.
Shows how far the derivation vote ever moves the odds from the base rate, which the registry note says to expect it rarely does.

Holding the contract through the same folds is the only same-series trading reference, so this gap shows whether trading the side with more derivations earned more than simply holding, after the costs that every change of the vote's side pays.

A trade closes only when the derivation vote changes the side of the curve-mapped call, so this count shows how often the program's derivations actually changed the side, and every trading figure for this model is read beside it.
Shows how one-sided the derivation vote plus the validation-fitted curve is; a share at or near one or zero means the curve's intercept, which decides every tied bar, is making nearly every call.

The search over the induced feature count, the atom order, the minimum fire count, the rule count, the smoothing pseudo count and the evidence predicate count is scored by the shared tuning objective, an optimistic selection score to be read beside the fold's test value.

Not computed: this model has no price model, so there is no forecast move to compare with the actual move.
Not computed: this model has no price model, so there is no forecast sign to score.

caveats: The single fit logs one validation logarithmic loss for the epoch, measured on the same validation rows that fitted the curve's slope and intercept, and no training value because the logic program fit returns no loss.

constraint_satisfaction.summary: The bar's side (long or short) under hard constraints from high-confidence rules (solved by python-constraint) and weighted soft constraints from reliable predicates.
constraint_satisfaction.implementationNote: Bridge: score = soft-CSP cost of short minus cost of long (violated weights plus an infeasibility penalty), calibrated on validation. Differs from the spec: the spec checks feasibility; P(up) is the train-span up-rate of its output, calibrated on validation, with one decision variable per bar and no portfolio sizing. Expect: probabilities near the base rate.

induced_feature_count.label: Induced feature predicates
induced_feature_count.description: Feature columns turned into two predicates each (above the training 2/3 quantile, below the 1/3 quantile), chosen by how differently their tails moved on the training span.

atom_order.label: Conditions per mined rule
atom_order.description: Largest number of predicates in one mined rule (1: single conditions, 2: pairs).

minimum_fire_count.label: Minimum firings
minimum_fire_count.description: A mined rule must have fired on at least this many training bars.

rule_count.label: Rules kept
rule_count.description: Rules kept after ranking by how far their training up-rate sits from the base rate.

smoothing_pseudo_count.label: Smoothing pseudo-count
smoothing_pseudo_count.description: Pseudo-bars at the base rate added to every training rate (Laplace-style smoothing).

hard_constraint_confidence.label: Hard-constraint confidence
hard_constraint_confidence.description: A rule becomes a hard constraint when its training up-rate is at least this far from even odds.

infeasible_side_penalty.label: Infeasibility penalty
infeasible_side_penalty.description: Cost added to a side the hard constraints exclude.

native.produces: One complete assignment of a value to every variable that breaks none of the stated constraints, or a definitive report that no such assignment exists.
native.targetVariable: Whether a jointly feasible combination of position sizes exists under the margin limit, the per-instrument caps and the correlated-exposure limit, and which combination it is
native.objectiveNote: Nothing is fitted: arc-consistency propagation prunes each variable's domain and backtracking search then looks for any assignment that satisfies every constraint, so there is no loss and no learned parameter.

metrics.why: The solver's whole answer is whether a feasible assignment exists, so the share of bars on which backtracking search finds one shows whether the constraint set is so tight it never allows a trade or so loose it allows everything.
metrics.baseline: A solver given no constraints at all on the same bars, which allows every combination of position sizes

metrics.why: A returned assignment is only an answer if the margin limit, the caps and the exposure limit all hold on it, so the largest remaining violation should be exactly zero for the hard version and is the cost being minimised in the weighted version.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value of an assignment that satisfies every hard constraint

metrics.why: Backtracking is exponential in the worst case, so the count of propagation passes and of backed-up assignments, with whether the search finished or hit its depth limit, tells whether a report of no solution is a proof or only a search that stopped.

When the account state behind the margin and exposure limits moves from one period to the next, this shows how often the same binding constraints and the same feasible assignment come back, which is what makes the solution usable as a standing rule.

notApplicable.name: Regime Log-Likelihood
notApplicable.why: A constraint solver assigns no probability to any bar and contains no regimes, so a regime likelihood never existed for this model.

notApplicable.name: Regime Separation Index
notApplicable.why: Nothing in variables, domains and constraints partitions bars into regimes, so there is nothing to separate.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: The solver has no fitted score whose variance could be attributed to hyperparameters; its settings only govern search speed.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: Feasibility is not an additive prediction, so feature attributions and their stability are undefined for a constraint solver.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: The native output is an assignment or a report of infeasibility, not a stated probability, so calibration does not apply natively.

notApplicable.name: Regime Persistence Ratio
notApplicable.why: There is no regime label whose run length could be measured, because the solver keeps no state between problems.

notApplicable.name: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
notApplicable.why: A feasible assignment is not a score that ranks bars from most bearish to most bullish, so natively there is nothing to rank.

asRun.standInNote: The specification searches for a jointly feasible set of position sizes across instruments and forecasts nothing; the runnable adapter instead gives each bar one variable, the side, long or short, turns strongly one-sided mined or authored rules into hard constraints and every directional predicate into a weighted soft constraint, and scores the bar by the cost of short minus the cost of long. Every as-run number therefore measures that cost margin after a logistic curve fitted on validation rows, not feasibility of a portfolio.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is an unweighted logistic curve, fitted by maximum likelihood on the fold's validation rows only, of the soft-constraint cost of short minus the cost of long, where each side's cost is the summed log-odds weights of the predicates it contradicts plus the infeasible side penalty when the hard constraints exclude it.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per scored validation bar, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: The curve is unweighted, so this grades the stated odds that come from the cost margin plus the validation-fitted slope and intercept, against quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.

The logistic curve is monotone, so this ranking score is unchanged by its fitted scale and tests the cost margin itself: do bars where short violates more constraint weight than long go up more often.
A bounded score of the same curve-mapped margin, useful because the infeasible side penalty can push a few bars to very confident odds that dominate the logarithmic loss.
The slope and intercept were fitted on the validation span, so a slope away from one on the test span shows the cost margin's scale drifted between the two spans.
Because the curve is unweighted its odds are anchored to the validation up share, so the binned gap is a fair check of the margin plus curve, read with the count of occupied bins.
This is what trading the cheaper side of the soft constraints earned after costs under the engine's rule of following the latest call and filling at the next open.
Return per unit of bar-to-bar swing from trading the side the constraints prefer; zero is an arithmetic marker, not a no-skill level, because a random side still pays costs.
The deepest fall of equity while following the constraint solver's side, which shows the path a trader would have sat through.
Winning dollars over losing dollars across trades opened when the preferred side flipped; one is an arithmetic marker only.
Share of closed trades that made money when the side came from the constraint costs, read together with the trade count because a kept same-side call opens no new trade.
Hit rate of the hard call cut at 0.5, which depends on the validation-fitted intercept as much as on which side the constraints prefer.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and on down bars, so a curve whose intercept leans every call one way cannot look good from the base rate alone.
One symmetric number for whether the cheaper side agrees with the realised direction across all four cells of the confusion table.

Every single predicate, and every pair of predicates when the atom order parameter allows pairs, is scored on the training span before the hard constraints are chosen, so this count is the multiple-testing exposure behind them.
Shows whether the cost margin ever moves the curve away from the base rate, which the registry note says to expect it rarely does.

Holding the contract through the same folds is the only same-series trading reference, so this gap shows whether trading the side with the lower constraint cost earned more than simply holding, after the costs that every side flip pays.

A trade closes only when the cheaper side flips from long to short or back, so this count shows how often the soft constraints actually changed the side, and every trading figure for this model is read beside it.
Shows how one-sided the cost margin plus the validation-fitted curve is; a share at or near one or zero means the curve's intercept, not the constraints, is making nearly every call.
